name: Sequoia: Scalable, Robust, and Hardware-aware Speculative Decoding
problem: Existing speculative-decoding methods cannot scale to large speculation budgets and do not adapt to differing hyperparameters or to different hardware.
mechanism: Three components. (1) A DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING algorithm finds the optimal token TREE STRUCTURE for a given speculation budget, making tree shape optimal rather than hand-designed. (2) A novel sampling-and-VERIFICATION method that is robust across decoding TEMPERATURES - most prior work is tuned for greedy/low temperature and degrades badly at high temperature, which is a genuine production gap. (3) A HARDWARE-AWARE tree OPTIMIZER that automatically selects tree size and depth for the specific hardware platform, by measuring hardware characteristics rather than assuming them.
speedup_reported: Decoding speedup up to 4.04x (Llama2-7B), 3.73x (Llama2-13B), and 2.27x (Vicuna-33B) on an A100. Separately, in the OFFLOADING setting on L40, 0.56 s/token for exact Llama2-70B inference, which the authors report as 9.96x over their own optimized offloading system (5.6 s/token), 9.7x over DeepSpeed-Zero-Inference, and 19.5x over HuggingFace Accelerate. The L40 offloading figure is the interesting one and is the reason this paper is in the repo: it is a per-token LATENCY figure in seconds, not a unitless multiplier, so it is directly comparable to the repo's benchmark records.
notes:
ADOPTION: research-only - the hardware-aware tree optimiser is not in any production engine, and the temperature-robust verification algorithm is not adopted upstream. VENUE NOTE: no venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar; the arXiv comment field carries no venue claim, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = ArXiv v1 (Feb 2024). CAVEATS A READER MUST CARRY: the 9.96x is against the AUTHORS' OWN optimized offloading system, so it measures their tree optimiser against their own stack, not against the absence of speculative decoding - exactly the trap the xwind record in this repo documents for a different paper. The 4.04x/3.73x/2.27x series also declines monotonically with model size, which is the honest shape of the result: bigger target models amortise the draft pass better. Sequoia is the only record here where hardware_relevance is load-bearing in the mechanism itself rather than merely in the evaluation. DANGLING REF RESOLVED 2026-10-04 by reading the paper (arXiv:2402.12374v1), and it CORRECTS THE OLD SHORTHAND'S FORM FACTOR. The setup section names the exact part: "We evaluate SEQUOIA on different hardware including on-device experiments on L40 and A100(-PCIE 80GB) GPUs, as well as offloading experiments on an L40 GPU (with PCIE4)". Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.12374 . The paper's on-device results that this record's speedup claim rests on are the A100 runs (Table 1 'On-device results (A100)', Figure 7, Figure 8 forward-pass timings). So the card is the 80 GB PCIE, i.e. nvidia-a100-80gb-pcie, not the SXM4 part the old shorthand implied.
